Chamber Supports Complete Streets Ordinance 
Albuquerque City Council Bill No. O-14-27 
 
The Board of Directors of the Greater Albuquerque Chamber of Commerce strongly 
supports the Complete Streets ordinance (O-14-27) legislation introduced by Albuquerque 
City Councilor Issac Benton.  
  
The Complete Streets Ordinance establishes a new city-wide goal to expand safe use of 
Albuquerque’s streets by requiring equal consideration of the efficiency and safety of all 
types of travel. The ordinance will also adopt nationally-recognized standards for streets to 
serve existing and future development with appropriate infrastructure that encourages 
walkability and inviting public spaces. The Complete Streets approach is a nationally 
recognized framework for designing context-sensitive street facilities that enable safe travel 
by all users, including the estimated one third of Americans who do not drive.  Hundreds of 
municipalities and more than half of U.S. states have adopted ordinances and policies 
incorporating Complete Streets Concepts. To date, over 650 agencies at the local, regional 
and state-level have adopted Complete Streets policies. 
  
The Greater Albuquerque Chamber of Commerce believes that in order for Albuquerque to 
be competitive in a national economy, we must create a city infrastructure designed and 
operated to enable safe access for all users. The Complete Streets ordinance will benefit all 
pedestrians, cyclists, transit riders, and motorists. Creating communities that are safer and 
more attractive to pedestrians and cyclists is a critical component to advancing 
Albuquerque’s place as an innovative city.  The Complete Streets ordinance will also 
support high traffic areas in becoming more inclusive of all forms of urban transportation,

Greater Albuquerque 
Chamber of Commerce 
 
BOARD POSITION 
 
115 Gold Avenue SW, Suite 201 Albuquerque, NM 87102  (505) 764-3700  (505) 764-3714  
 
 
Background 
  
Albuquerque City Councilor Isaac Benton introduced the Complete Streets Ordinance (O-
14-27) at a regularly scheduled Albuquerque City Council meeting on Monday, October 6, 
2014. The Ordinance is open to comments and modifications prior to final action. The first 
formal hearing on the bill was heard on Wednesday, November 12 in the Land Use Planning 
& Zoning Committee (LUPZ).  A second hearing will be held in LUPZ on December 10, 
2014, with anticipated final action on the bill during the regularly scheduled Albuquerque 
City Council meeting on December 15, 2014.  The Mid Region Council of Governments has 
passed a resolution requiring that Complete Streets Principles are to be incorporated into the 
Council of Governments Planning Documents.
